title: Climbing Stairs II
summary: You climb a staircase with n+1 steps, each having a cost.
statement: You climb a staircase with n+1 steps, each having a cost. From step i, you can jump to i+1, i+2, or i+3, with a cost of (j-i)^2 added to the current step's cost. Starting from step 0 with zero cost, find the minimum total cost to reach step n.
constraints: n equals the length of costs and is at most 100,000.
Landing on step i pays costs[i-1]; step zero is free.
Each jump advances one, two, or three steps and additionally costs the square of its length.
hints: Only the cheapest cost of reaching each earlier step matters.
For step i, try the at most three predecessors i-1, i-2, and i-3.
Add the landing cost and squared jump length to each predecessor state and keep the minimum.
Every valid path reaches i from exactly one of those predecessors, so the recurrence is exhaustive and optimal.
